item.title: Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen to have penalties
item.description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will all have grid penalties at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will all have grid penalties at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Verstappen will start from the back of the grid while Hamilton and Leclerc will both have 10-place penalties.

They join Mercedes driver George Russell in having penalties for using too many engine parts. Russell's drop is only five places.

Verstappen will have an an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice.

Leclerc, Hamilton and Russell have all fitted new internal combustion engines.

The penalties for the Ferrari drivers are bigger than Russell's because it is the first time they have exceeded the limit of four engines per season, while Russell had already gone beyond that.

Verstappen famously won the 2024 Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race.

Rain is predicted overnight from Saturday into Sunday in the city this year, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day.

Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035.

F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035.

"The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo.

"The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil."

item.title: Tongue ruled out of Australia tour as Rashid stars in warm-up
item.description: England fast bowler Josh Tongue is ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury.

The 28-year-old suffered the injury in Pakistan last month and didn't take part in the final two games of that tri-series.

He will now return to the UK for further assessment and miss the one-day and T20 matches in Australia, which start with an ODI in Perth on 13 November.

Tongue, who has taken 46 wickets in 17 matches this year, is likely to be back for the three-match Test series in South Africa in December, with the squad set to be named next week.

The white-ball tour of Australia will mark the first time England have played down under since the 2025-26 Ashes demolition.

Coach Brendon McCullum had previously said he wanted a strong team for the ODI leg of the trip to Australia in the build-up to the World Cup in southern Africa next year.

The New Zealander also conceded he would have to rotate his squad for the T20 leg, given England's schedule in a busy winter of five separate overseas tours.

Rashid stars in warm-up win

Adil Rashid took four wickets as England beat Western Australia by 92 runs in their one-day warm-up match in Perth.

The 38-year-old was left out of the final three matches of the October tour of Pakistan and Sri Lanka but highlighted his importance down under, taking 4-35.

Fast bowler Jofra Archer chipped in with 3-34 as England ultimately cruised to victory.

It wasn't all straightforward though as a sloppy batting display saw England bowled out for 251.

Ben Duckett top scored with 49 while Liam Dawson was unbeaten for 44.

The hosts had England in trouble as they reached 60-1 before Rashid took a flurry of wickets, including Jayden Goodwin and Ashton Turner in successive deliveries.

Archer finished off the Western Australia tail, bowling them out for 159 and securing the win.

item.title: Rahm edges ahead of Hatton & McIlroy in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jon Rahm leads Tyrrell Hatton and Francesca Laporta by one shot, and Rory McIlroy by two, after the third round of the Abu Dhabi Championship.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Abu Dhabi Championship third-round leaderboard

-18 J Rahm (Spa); -17 T Hatton (Eng), F Laporta (Ita); -16 R McIlroy (NI); -15 A Scott (Aus); -14 M Jordan (Eng), D Puig (Spa)

Selected others: -12 S Bairstow (Eng), N Kimsey (Eng); -11 T Fleetwood (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), A Sullivan (Eng); -9 A Rai (Eng); -8 E Chacarra (Spa), M Wallace (Eng); -1 P Reed (US)

Jon Rahm has a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship but Ryder Cup team-mates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy are in close contention.

The 31-year-old Spaniard shared the overnight lead with Italy's Francesco Laporta and fellow former LIV player Hatton, but moved clear of them both with a six-under-par 66 at Yas Links on Saturday.

Hatton and Laporta both carded a 67, as did McIlroy, who goes into the final round in fourth place on 16 under.

Rahm, who said recently that he does not know what 2027 holds after quitting the LIV tour, is aiming for a first solo tournament triumph since winning the Masters in 2023.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy remains in hot pursuit, however, after bouncing back in spectacular fashion since being given a two-shot penalty in the opening round for improving his lie before taking a chip shot.

The six-time major winner hit 11 birdies in a second-round 63 and another eight in his third round, but a double bogey six at the par-four 10th - and another dropped shot at the 17th - left McIlroy two shots off the lead.

And he acknowledges that it will take something special on the final day to reel in Rahm and co.

"There are low ones [scores] out there and I am going to have to shoot a low one - something in the mid to low 60s - to get it done tomorrow and that will be the goal," said McIlroy.

Hatton, meanwhile, is looking forward to going head-to-head again with Rahm after playing alongside the two-time major champion, and Laporta, in Saturday's final group.

All three will play together once again on Sunday.

"Obviously final group tomorrow there's a lot to play for," said Hatton, who briefly moved level with Rahm at the top of the leaderboard in the third round after holing his seventh birdie of the day on the 14th.

"Naturally we are going to want to beat each other. Hopefully I can get off to a good start and put him under some pressure."

Rahm, who is chasing his first win in the Abu Dhabi Championship, responded well after being put under pressure by Hatton on Saturday.

He reclaimed the outright lead on the 15th with a superb, curling 20-foot birdie putt and came close to extending his advantage at the last, just coming up short with another birdie chance as he finished without a single dropped shot.

Laporta also produced a bogey-free round to keep pace with the field's big hitters as the 36-year-old, who shot 10 under par to claim a first-round lead, bids for a first title on the DP World Tour.

Elsewhere, Australian Adam Scott remained bogey-free for the tournament after three rounds and moved up to fifth place on 15 under with a 66.

And Englishman Matthew Jordan is a shot further back, alongside Spain's David Puig, after a third-round 69.

item.title: Scotland lose Welsh and call up Porteous
item.description: Swansea City centre-back Stephen Welsh drops out the Scotland squad for their forthcoming Nations League double-header and is replaced with Los Angeles' Ryan Porteous.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Swansea City centre-back Stephen Welsh has dropped out the Scotland squad for their forthcoming Nations League double-header and been replaced with Los Angeles' Ryan Porteous.

Fears that Welsh had sustained serious knee ligament damage, following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Swansea's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth on Tuesday, appeared to have eased on Thursday.

A scan showed the 26-year-old had not suffered a significant problem and Swansea hoped he could even play some part of their game at Birmingham City on Saturday.

But the Scottish FA has now announced his withdrawal from their matches at home to North Macedonia on Friday and away to Switzerland on Monday, 16 November.

Welsh has earned all four of his caps since Sebastien Pocognoli was appointed Scotland head coach in the summer.

Porteous, 27, last played for Scotland under Steve Clarke in March 2025, coming on as a late substitute to win his 13th cap in a 1-0 Nations League play-off win in Greece.

The former Hibernian defender left Watford for Los Angeles last August, having finished the previous season on loan to Preston, and has made 35 appearances this year for the side sitting sixth in the Western Conference and 12th in the overall Major League Soccer (MLS) table.

Scotland must take at least four points from their final two group games to have a chance of making the promotion play-offs.

item.title: Kiwis reap rewards of gamble on 'freak of nature' Ponga
item.description: Kalyn Ponga's return to Rugby League World Cup action, just 23 days after breaking his arm, was a risk. But New Zealand head coach Stacey Jones felt it was a risk worth taking - and was proved right.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

"He's a tough character and he was so adamant he was playing."

Kalyn Ponga, in the words of his head coach Stacey Jones, was never going to miss New Zealand's Rugby League World Cup semi-final.

But it was a remarkable return to action for a player whose tournament turned from dream to nightmare just over three weeks ago.

In the World Cup opener against Australia in Sydney on 15 October, Ponga seemed to be enjoying a perfect New Zealand debut. Then it all went wrong.

The 28-year-old scored two second-half tries but was forced off late in the game - having played for 20 minutes with a broken left forearm sustained in a tackle with Cameron Munster. The Kiwis went on to lose 24-22; Ponga required surgery.

Just 23 days later, their talismanic full-back – initially named as a reserve, and then on the interchange bench – made a shock return to the starting 13 and delivered a starring performance as New Zealand overpowered Tonga 34-10 to reach their first Men's Rugby League World Cup final for 13 years.

"Where sports science is these days – I saw what he had in his arm, the rod or plate was covering his whole arm," Jones said.

"We didn't know until after our second-to-last training that he was going to be all right – he ticked all the boxes. Just a tough person."

Playing with black protective bandaging taped to his left forearm, Ponga was directly involved in four of New Zealand's six tries. His fancy footwork and slick handling setting up scores for Briton Nikora, Casey McLean and Xavier Willison.

He largely dominated the contest with opposite number Lehi Hopoate, notably clearing out the full-back as he fumbled a grubber kick in Tonga's in-goal area for New Zealand's second try, scored by Dane Gagai.

In defence, a bruising try-saving block on Demitric Vaimauga indicated no cause for concern about his wounded wing.

"Obviously a freak of a player," said Kiwis captain James Fisher-Harris. "The defensive mindset he had tonight, he saved a couple of tries. That's what I love about KP.

"He's a freak of nature. His leadership skills are underrated. He's really good for us, our spine especially."

But while it was undoubtedly the Ponga show at the home of his NRL side Newcastle Knights, New Zealand are not just a one-man band.

Gagai sparked the counter-attack for McLean's try by forcing a knock-on around halfway. Jahrome Hughes added directness with his carries and when putting boot to ball. Dead-eye kicker Jamayne Isaako mastered fierce winds to kick five out of six conversions, curling two over from the left touchline, to take his tally for the tournament to 36 from 38 attempts.

Asked if this was New Zealand's best shot at adding a second title to their 2008 triumph, Fisher-Harris paused before replying: "Yes."

"We're just trying to chase history," he added. "We've only done it once but we've been building with this squad, this generation, for the past six or seven years."

'Missed opportunity' but Tonga not blaming weather

For 48 minutes, New Zealand and Tonga played with the intensity and fever of two sides seemingly locked on course for the drama of a golden-point extra-time finish.

Then the Kiwis' relentless pressure told, with two tries in five minutes extending their lead to 14 points and turning a contest into a procession.

The weather in Newcastle impacted the match from kick-off but deteriorated dramatically in the second half, with Tonga toiling in the face of howling wind and rain – conditions best encapsulated by a restart blowing back into their own half.

But head coach Kristian Woolf did not use this an excuse for his side's defeat by New Zealand, stating his team "didn't handle the conditions as well as they did".

Unbeaten through the group stage, Tonga lacked direction in attack, were guilty of poor decision-making at the end of sets, and looked vulnerable defending a bouncing ball.

"It was a disappointing way to finish. Whoever was against the wind in the second half was going to find it tough and we just had to handle it better," said Woolf.

"It's a bit of a missed opportunity with what the group's been able to do, how talented the group is, some of the footy we've played, but we just couldn't get it done tonight."

Putting the result into perspective, with Tonga playing in the semi-finals for just the second time, Woolf added: "Once upon a time, we were just happy to be in the finals and be competitive. Now, we see ourselves as real players and believe we can win it.

"We thought we could do that tonight. We certainly think we've got a team that is capable of doing that. Tongan rugby league can be really confident going forward."

New Zealand women 'hungry' for success

The last time New Zealand had teams in both the men's and women's finals on Australian soil, they walked away with two trophies.

The year was 2008. For the men, it was a maiden title; for the women, a third consecutive crown. Neither side has lifted the trophy since then, losing a combined four finals. In Brisbane next Sunday, a nation will be hoping history repeats itself.

New Zealand women maintained their 100% record of reaching the trophy match with a controlled 32-0 win over Samoa, spearheaded by a hat-trick for dual-code international Stacey Waaka.

But although yet to lose in the tournament, and having conceded just 24 points across four matches, New Zealand know they will face a stiff challenge from either three-time defending champions Australia or Fiji in the final.

"The tournament has been around building. How we started [an 18-12 win over Fiji] wasn't how we wanted to start – we got tested early, faced some adversity and challenges which will help us next week," said captain Georgia Hale.

"It's a challenge we are hungry for. The focus will be really internal, it's around our pack, our threat, what we can control, what we believe in. It will be a huge task but one we've been working towards for four years."

item.title: Ireland going from strength to strength - Murray
item.description: Former Ireland scrum-half Conor Murray says on the Ireland Rugby Social that he is impressed with how the Irish squad is progressing and their strength in depth.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Ireland began their autumn series of Nations Championship matches by scoring six tries in a comprehensive 42-12 win over Argentina at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Friday night.

Afterwards on the Ireland Rugby Social podcast, BBC Sport NI's Gavin Andrews spoke to Ireland second row Joe McCarthy about his thoughts on the game and then chatted to co-presenter and former Ireland scrum-half Conor Murray to break down the analysis of the home side's performance.

With matches against Fiji and South Africa to follow over the next couple of weeks, there was much to dissect after the win over the Pumas and assess what may be to come for the remainder of November.

You can watch the podcast now on BBC NI YouTube, external or listen on BBC Sounds.

Here are a few highlights of what Murray had to say.

On Hugo Keenan, who scored a hat-trick of tries: "Hugo stood out but he's always going to do that. He talks so much on the pitch and makes it way easier for the players around him.

"He's always marshalling the wingers and that kind of back-field system. That's Hugo in a nutshell. He's the ultimate team player.

"He looked incredibly fit, incredibly quick, explosive. He looked back to his best."

On fledgling half-back partnership Sam Prendergast and Craig Casey: "Craig and Sam marshalled the game really well. Not that there were question marks but they were a relatively new combination and it was their first time getting a big Test start together.

"Sam can forget what he's been through, I suppose the rocky start to his international career and the public scrutiny on him.

"He looks like a player who has just soaked it all in and is using it as a weapon now. He looked really sharp. He looks like he has bulked up, which is great to see too.

"There'll be a target on his back, there was already but there definitely will be now as he is such a big influence.

"We know what Craig Casey can do in terms of quick ball and magical moments but now in terms of the control of the game.

"His passing was on the money and his kicking is top notch. The overall control is probably the test that Andy Farrell gave him. He knows what he can do in loose play but in terms of controlling a Test game I thought the half-backs were brilliant."

On an impressive performance by the forwards: "[Tadhg] Furlong went really well, he's always a standard-bearer anyhow and you get top-notch performances from him, but [Andrew] Porter, another player who came back from an extended period out with injury, he's come back and showed what he's about.

"His explosiveness in open play and his fitness, he's like another back row on the field.

"Dan Sheehan, Tadhg Beirne, Joe McCarthy, Ryan Baird, the back row, across the board, all really good. I think Nick Timoney and Josh [van der Flier] are in a real battle as regards that number seven jersey."

On strength in depth: "The depth we have now is really impressive. Over a year ago there were a good few injuries and people were worrying, not that there was panic, but wondering, 'where's the depth?' Not that we had no depth, but Andy had to blood a few players quickly.

"Those players are now in the squad and they are pushing lads across the board, pushing the other boys to perform.

"I think Irish rugby is going from strength to strength and it's really impressive to see."

On facing Fiji next week and then South Africa: "They [Ireland] should beat Fiji. I don't think that's getting ahead of ourselves. I think that's where Ireland rugby is at now.

"The lads coming in next week will be thinking they have a chance to perform and will want to be in Andy and the coaches' minds for selection for the South Africa game.

"That's how competitive the squad is. It's a real difference now that the guys coming out against Fiji aren't just saying, 'I'm getting a run out here', but rather, 'I'm actually in the mix here', which is really healthy.

"Lads deserve a chance but Andy will expect the same level of performance. When there are changes, there can be a dip because the combinations change but it's a big week of prep now and those guys will sniff an opportunity that they can stay involved.

"They won't say it but everyone wants to be involved against South Africa.

"There'll still be a core to the team that will be really, really strong, because you respect Fiji and you want some sort of consistency and some sort of momentum."

item.title: My dream is to win Ballon d'Or - Gabriel
item.description: Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel says his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or", as he closes in on a move to Real Madrid.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel says his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or", as he closes in on a move to Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old is still registered at United but has been training on his own in Spain after walking out on the club and relocating with his family.

He has subsequently reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid but no deal has been signed as yet.

On Friday, following one of his sessions, the teenager was approached by Spanish news outlet Marca who presented him with a copy of their newspaper, which featured a front-page story about his expected move to Los Blancos.

The newspaper reported he told them in English: "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or."

United would be due compensation should Gabriel leave, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League.

Though no club-to-club talks have been held, sources have told BBC Sport that Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives.

Despite United having Gabriel's registration domestically, it is not thought it could prevent the youngster joining a club overseas as he now has a European Union passport through his mother, who has Cypriot origin.

While Real and United are both in the Uefa Youth League this season, competition rules prevent players from appearing for more than one club in a single season and Gabriel scored a hat-trick in his final appearance for United against Sabah in September.

He was named the Premier League's Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season began.

item.title: Ponga-inspired New Zealand reach World Cup final
item.description: Kalyn Ponga returns from a broken arm to inspire New Zealand to victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reach their first World Cup final since 2013.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

New Zealand (12) 34

Tries: Nikora, Gagai, McLean, Hughes, Willison, Nicoll-Klokstad Goals: Isaako 5

Tonga (10) 10

Tries: Fifita 2 Goals: Katoa

Just 23 days after breaking his arm, Kalyn Ponga returned to inspire New Zealand to a 34-10 victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reached their first World Cup final since 2013.

Ponga had been named initially in reserve and then as one of the interchange players in the build-up to this contest - and the expectation was that he would be eased back into action and play a limited role.

Instead, head coach Stacey Jones stunned many with his decision to include Ponga in New Zealand's starting 13 but was repaid in full as the Newcastle Knights talisman starred on home turf at the McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales,

Ponga's impact from full-back was almost immediate as he sent Briton Nikora over in the right corner inside four minutes.

He was also involved in the Kiwis' second try of the game - as his contest with his opposite number Lehi Hopoate was crucial to Dane Gagai grounding the ball.

And while the swirling wind made conditions almost unplayable at times, he repeatedly gathered high kicks and made several telling defensive contributions.

One of those included throwing himself in the way of Tonga's juggernaut second row Demitric Vaimauga to prevent a certain try, while his ability to stall Hopoate's run and prevent him from offloading to Isaiya Katoa stopped another at a key stage with New Zealand only 12-10 ahead.

The prelude to this fixture was almost every bit as gripping as the main event.

Tonga's traditional war dance, the Sipi Tau, was met by New Zealand's Haka and a long stand-off between the players provided the perfect backdrop to a contest brimming with athleticism, power and superb ball-handling skills.

For the second week running, Tonga fans turned out in force with the stands a sea of red.

And they witnessed their side's participation in a wonderful advert for rugby league with Jojo Fifita scoring two excellent tries.

However, the match ultimately swung away from them in a five-minute period after the break when New Zealand's outstanding centre Casey McLean surged over in the left corner and the wily Jahrome Hughes darted in to score.

On this occasion, Kristian Woolf's team, who effectively torpedoed England's hopes of reaching the last four with a 30-12 in their opening match on 17 October, were unable to stage the same sort of fightback that helped them defeat their Pacific Island rivals Samoa last weekend.

With the scoreboard, time and a gale-force wind against Tonga, Xavier Willison punished them further when they failed to gather a short drop out.

And when Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad superbly grounded Erin Clark's kick, it put the gloss on a fine New Zealand performance.

item.title: New Zealand sweep aside Samoa to reach Women's World Cup final
item.description: New Zealand's women will hope it is fourth time lucky after defeating Samoa 32-0 to reach next Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

New Zealand (8) 32

Tries: Wiki, Waaka 3, Hufanga, Atai, McGregor Goals: Kiria-Ratu 2

Samoa (0) 0

New Zealand's women will hope it is fourth time lucky after defeating Samoa 32-0 to reach next Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final.

It will be the Kiwi Ferns' seventh successive appearance in the showpiece match, but having won the first three between 2000-2008, three trips to the final since then have all ended in heartache.

Three consecutive losses to Australia included a blowout 54-4 scoreline four years ago at Old Trafford and unless debutants Fiji spring one of the greatest upsets in the tournament's history in the other semi-final, the Jillaroos are likely to again provide the substantial obstacle to New Zealand becoming four-time champions.

However, on Saturday, New Zealand made light of the blustery and difficult conditions inside Newcastle's McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, to make their case as potential winners.

Mackenzie Wiki's try - less than two minutes into proceedings, off the back of a Samoa error - set the tone for the Kiwi Ferns.

As the storm clouds began to gather overhead, New Zealand's dual-code international Stacey Waaka capitalised on some indecision from Samoa winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala to collect and ground Raecene McGregor's kick.

It was efficient and highly professional from New Zealand, who conceded just 24 points across their three group games and once again exhibited their defensive parsimony during a hard-fought first period.

A combination of that and Samoa's inability to make the most of field position, with a smattering of handling errors thrown in as well, laid the platform for New Zealand's triumph.

There were notable bright spots for the Samoa fans to enjoy.

Fanua Rimoni was a powerful and dominant presence at lock forward, while teenage winger Anastasia Leatupue produced a nerveless showing on her international bow.

Samoa's biggest disappointment was that they could not get the ball into the hands of the 18-year-old in good attacking positions - with Pauline Piliae-Rasabale twice pulled up for forward passes on the right edge in an error-strewn display.

But just like in the first 35 minutes, they had no answer to New Zealand's more potent attacking threat.

Waaka was again the beneficiary of a pinpoint McGregor kick as she crossed for her second try and Mele Hufanga held off the attentions of three Samoa defenders tfor her score.

It was a feat that was matched by Kaiyah Atai just over two minutes later as New Zealand went through the gears.

With Samoa's resistance gradually waning, Waaka capped a fine individual display with her hat-trick and McGregor scored the try her performance richly deserved to round off a fine New Zealand display.

Matt's player of the match: Stacey Waaka

It takes a big performance to steal the limelight away from the blockbusting Mele Hufanga in the Kiwis back-line but cross-code star Stacey Waaka did just that with an impressive display.

She cut Samoa open with searing breaks, cranking out 131 metres, and ran in a hat-trick - including a perfectly timed run to collect Raecene McGregor's deft kick - added to two line breaks and line break assists, a try assist and three tackle breaks.

New Zealand took their time to get going, and Waaka's influence was key to making that step.

item.title: Buatsi v Hutchinson 2 - world light-heavyweight title fight predictions
item.description: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's light-heavyweight world title fight between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson renew their rivalry for the vacant WBC world light-heavyweight title in Manchester on Saturday.

The British rivals first met in a highly entertaining, hard-fought contest on the undercard of Daniel Dubois' win over Anthony Joshua in September 2024.

Londoner Buatsi, 33, twice knocked down Hutchinson before going on to win by split decision.

Scotland's Hutchinson, 28, suffered the second defeat of his professional career that night but two wins since have put him in a position to fight for a first world title.

Can Buatsi repeat his victory? Or will Hutchinson gain revenge in Manchester?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from across the boxing world to get their predictions.

Chantelle Cameron - two-weight world champion

"Buatsi may stop him this time in the later rounds. I think he gets it done between rounds nine and 12."

Prediction - Buatsi

David Allen - British heavyweight

"Willy has improved massively since the first fight, whereas I'm not sure I could say the same for Joshua."

Prediction - Hutchinson

Carl Frampton - former world champion

"It's a really good fight. I think the first fight was very good - Willy was dropped a couple of times in the fight and that cost him. Otherwise, his performance was OK. He's matured a lot since that fight and is in good form.

"Buatsi has maybe just started to look old but the fact the world title is on the line... When he turned professional, everyone thought he was a shoo-in to become world champion and he hasn't achieved it yet. This is the chance, so we may see a level of Buatsi that we haven't seen in a while.

"I think it'll be really competitive but I'm just edging Hutchinson to win on points with the run of form he's on."

Prediction - Hutchinson

Viddal Riley - European cruiserweight champion

"Willy Hutchinson will get the win - it's his time. Buatsi is a tough fighter and it won't be easy but when I look at who is fresh and who has the bit between their teeth a little more - I'm backing Hutchinson."

Prediction - Hutchinson

Denzel Bentley - former WBO middleweight champion

"I'm going for a repeat for Buatsi and he finally gets his hands on a world title. It has been 10 years since he was at the Olympics and it felt like he slipped away from that batch of fighters.

"Buatsi does things in his own time and he's finally got his shot. It comes at a great time for him, it could go two ways - he's either overconfident because he's beaten Willy or his confidence could be a good thing and he could step on it early and I think it's the second one.

"I can't see Willy getting stopped - he's tough - so I'm going Buatsi on points, but he might get a knockdown."

Prediction - Buatsi

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"It's very rare people can turn the rematch around when they lose the first one. On that basis, I am going for Joshua Buatsi, possibly even by late stoppage."

Prediction - Buatsi

Zelfa Barrett - former European super-featherweight champion

"I'm going with Buatsi to win again. Hutchinson showed he was weak to the body and that could be his kryptonite.

"Hutchinson is a good fighter; he's slick and sharp, but I think Buatsi has his number and wins on points."

Prediction - Buatsi

Sam Jones - boxing manager

"Willy Hutchinson is in his physical and mental prime and I think he wins the fight. I've known Willy since he turned professional as an 18-year-old.

"He's always had the tools to be a world champion and I believe timing is everything in boxing. I believe he's also catching Buatsi at the right time."

Prediction - Hutchinson

Darren Barker - former middleweight world champion

"What a rematch. He showed his worth, his bottle and his ability did Willy Hutchinson in that first fight and proved a lot as a fighter.

"Joshua Buatsi had a very good fight with Callum Smith, although he came out second best. Not so impressive in his win over Zach Parker, it was a close fight so a lot of questions surround him and what's left.

"Hutchinson is a man in form and looks like a man who is matured both physically and mentally. This is a fantastic rematch with the WBC light-heavyweight title on the line. It promises to be an action-packed contest and the pot of gold is massive."

Prediction - Hutchinson

Ade Olapido - DAZN presenter

"A rematch that I didn't think would come around but it all makes sense with the added incentive of gold. Someone will leave as world champion. The first time they fought, it was 80-20 Buatsi for me, but Hutchinson was a lot better than I expected.

"He has now closed that gap drastically and now it's 55-45 Buatsi. How much has Callum Smith taken out of Buatsi? On the flip side, Hutchinson, after that defeat, has gone from strength to strength.

"He showed everything in his last fight against Ezra Taylor. I favour Buatsi just, but we'll see how much that Smith fight took out of him. I think Buatsi will be world champion, but I wouldn't be surprised if Willy Hutchinson walks home with gold."

Prediction - Buatsi

item.title: I had to play regularly for my mental wellbeing - Trafford on summer move
item.description: Leeds United's James Trafford opens up on his struggles at Manchester City last season that were behind his summer transfer.
item.content:encoded:
I had to play regularly for my mental wellbeing - Trafford on summer move

Leeds United's James Trafford opens up on his struggles at Manchester City last season that were behind his summer transfer.

item.title: Not playing at Man City 'horrendous' - Trafford
item.description: James Trafford says not playing for Manchester City last season was "horrendous" and left him with no choice but to leave the club and join Leeds United in the summer.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

James Trafford says not playing for Manchester City last season was "horrendous" before he moved to Leeds United in the summer in search of first-team football.

City re-signed academy graduate Trafford in July 2025, two years after he had left the club to join Championship side Burnley.

But less than six weeks after his arrival, Italy international Gianluigi Donnarumma arrived from Paris St-Germain.

The 27-year-old, who helped the French club win the Champions League just weeks earlier, immediately became City's first-choice goalkeeper, leaving Trafford short of playing time.

After starting the first three matches of the campaign, 24-year-old Trafford made just one further Premier League start in the 35 games that followed Donnarumma's arrival.

Speaking on Football Daily's The Football Interview, Trafford reflected on the difficulties he encountered during a season on the fringes of Pep Guardiola's squad.

"What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing," said Trafford.

"You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up.

"I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny."

Despite his limited playing time, Trafford believes he still gained plenty from his final season at City, having helped the club win the League Cup and FA Cup after starting both finals at Wembley.

"Going into any season, I always have the highest of hopes and always the belief that it will go the best way it could," he added.

"Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens.

"In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year.

"There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

'It's my aim to be England's number one'

Trafford was part of England's squad for the 2026 World Cup and, although he did not get game time, being part of Thomas Tuchel's squad was an "incredible experience" that he says he will not forget.

"I didn't play, but it is what it is," said Trafford. "I didn't expect to play when I got called up. I knew what my role was, but you just take as much experience as possible, learn from it and keep trying to win the day, because the more days you win, the better position you're in."

Next time around, though, Trafford hopes to be England's starting goalkeeper and believes that if he continues his impressive performances with Leeds, that ambition is entirely achievable.

"It's my aim and it's something I've always dreamed of," said Trafford.

"I always believe that one day I could be. Every day I try to keep improving to put myself in the best position to be England's number one one day.

"I think everyone in the goalkeeping department with the national team wants to be number one because it's an amazing position to be in."

'Leeds would love to get back into Europe'

After returning from the World Cup, Trafford left City to join Leeds United in a deal worth up to £45m - a record for a British goalkeeper.

Since arriving at Elland Road, he has relished the opportunity to play regularly in the Premier League.

The former Bolton Wanderers and Accrington Stanley loanee has started all nine of Leeds' Premier League matches this season, keeping three clean sheets, with only Brighton (seven) and Arsenal (five) having conceded fewer goals than Daniel Farke's side (eight).

His performances have helped Leeds to 12th in the table before this weekend's fixtures - just two points off the European places - and he says the club are only going to get better.

"I just think it's an incredible club," he said. "You look at the fanbase, everyone here - it's an incredible place. It's just somewhere that's only going and getting better.

"We'd love to get back into Europe. I think every club you ask would like to get into Europe, so the main goal is just to keep on improving."
